articles.title: VRT MAX arrives in Music Assistant
articles.dek: A first contribution brings Flemish public radio, podcasts, favourites and listening progress into Music Assistant.
body: Merged provider support will let Music Assistant connect directly to VRT MAX, the streaming service of the Flemish public broadcaster. Bram Goolaerts’ contribution covers live stations including Radio 1, Radio 2, Studio Brussel, MNM and Klara, alongside listen-back programmes, podcasts and search. Live radio will work without signing in.

Connecting an account adds on-demand playback, Mijn lijst library syncing and resume positions that carry across devices. The provider supports multiple instances, so people in one household can keep separate accounts, and listen-back episodes can expose played songs as chapters in Now Playing.
This is Goolaerts’ first merged contribution to the Music Assistant server. Welcome, Bram—and congratulations on landing an unusually complete first PR.

articles.title: The iOS energy widget makes room for gas and batteries
articles.dek: Home Assistant’s glanceable energy view now carries four parts of a household’s energy picture, including two-way battery flow.
body: Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves expanded the Home Assistant iOS energy widget beyond grid and solar. Battery discharge is stacked above the chart axis, charging below it, while gas appears as a separate figure because its statistics may be measured in volume rather than energy.

The merged widget update uses the same consumption math as the energy dashboard, so energy used to charge a battery is not counted as household demand. Cost combines electricity and gas, and all four sources still fit on the small widget and Lock Screen accessories.
The work continues Gonçalves’s August run on the widget, after Lock Screen sizing, a reload action for missing data and clearer period and refresh-time information landed earlier in the month.
articles.continuity: Part of a month-long series improving Home Assistant’s energy widgets across iPhone and Lock Screen layouts.

articles.title: ESPHome’s serial tools recognize devices beyond Wi‑Fi
articles.dek: A merged ESPHome change lets devices connected by Ethernet, Thread or a modem tell compatible serial tools how they are online and where to open their local web page.
body: ESPHome’s Improv Serial protocol lets a setup tool talk to a device over USB or another serial connection. Keith Burzinski’s change allows that protocol to run on devices without Wi‑Fi, including Ethernet-only boards, and report whether they are online and which network interfaces they have.

Compatible tools can also receive the device’s local web address. Wi‑Fi provisioning remains Wi‑Fi-only; the new support reports Ethernet, Thread and modem connections rather than configuring them. The same work stops tools from showing stale success while a device is still leaving its previous Wi‑Fi network.
articles.continuity: Builds on August work making ESPHome’s network stack more deliberate about multiple active interfaces.

articles.title: Bluetooth fix clears connections left by removed adapters
articles.dek: The merged repair drops connections that depended on a disabled or removed adapter, allowing devices to reconnect cleanly.
body: Radek Podgorny traced a stubborn Bluetooth state mismatch to scanner removal. Home Assistant cleared its bookkeeping when an adapter disappeared, but connections made through that adapter could remain alive, continuing to deliver notifications while occupying a slot the system believed was free.

The fix disconnects clients that still depend on an adapter when that adapter is removed, while leaving alone any device that has already found another route. It covers local adapters and ESPHome Bluetooth proxies.

Podgorny verified the local path on real BlueZ hardware: disabling the adapter dropped the kernel link, and enabling it again allowed a clean reconnect. The remote-proxy path has automated coverage but was not part of that hardware test.

articles.title: Konyks socket indicator setting lands
articles.dek: Merged library and Core changes expose an LED mode supported by two Konyks sockets even though Tuya’s published device information leaves it out.
body: New contributor minimicro34 added device definitions for the Konyks Priska Max 3 FR and Priska Duo FR. Both sockets support four indicator modes—including always on—even though Tuya’s metadata lists only relay, position and off.

A companion Home Assistant change supplies the readable translation for Tuya’s light-mode selector. Together, the three PRs carry the capability from device knowledge in the shared library through to a label users can understand in Home Assistant.
These are minimicro34’s first merged contributions to both tuya-device-handlers and Home Assistant Core. Welcome to both projects.

articles.title: Beta week protects the homes people already configured
articles.dek: From August 24–30, repairs across Home Assistant Core and the frontend preserved automations, replacement devices and compatibility with existing systems.
body: From Monday, August 24 through Sunday, August 30, Home Assistant moved into beta with a clear theme: protect configurations and compatibility people already rely on. The work was spread across Core and the frontend, but each repair reduced the chance that an update would undo earlier setup or make established hardware behave differently.

Core reverted a NumPy update that broke Proxmox environments, validated stored KNX interface data before loading it, restored follow-up voice commands and corrected temperature-offset conversion for Matter thermostats. These fixes preserve compatibility rather than adding something new to configure.

In the frontend, one repair stopped editor state leaking when people switched between automations, scripts or scenes. Another kept the existing automation configuration when a device is replaced. Together, they protect work people have already put into their homes—the strongest common thread in the week’s beta fixes.
articles.continuity: The recap narrows the week to one reader outcome: preserving existing Home Assistant configuration and compatibility during beta.
